newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH SAY DFL10 BLN BORROWING REMAINS IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH SAY DFL10 BLN BORROWING REMAINS IN 1997.

text.p: The Dutch Finance Ministry's capital markets agency said on Wednesday that 10.0 billion guilders of its 1997 borrowing requirement remained.
The agency also said in its Spring Memorandum that the forecast 1997 Dutch budget deficit had been cut to 18.6 billion guilders from 21.0 billion previously.
It said it had also redeemed 6.8 billion guilders of state bonds early so far in 1997, but scheduled redemptions of bonds remained steady at 12.5 billion guilders.
The borrowing requirement for 1997 was increased to 37.9 billion guilders from 33.5 billion previously as the increase in early redemptions exceeded the cut in the budget deficit.
The agency also detailed the 27.9 billion guilder difference between the 1997 borrowing requirement and the total remaining funding.

It said a reduction of the ministry's cash balances at the central bank accounted for 14.4 billion guilders, the new 5.75 percent February 2007 bond issued in January raised 7.5 billion and tap issues of the 9.0 percent January 2001 and 7.5 percent January 2023 bonds brought another 6.0 billion guilders.
The agency has previously said it will announce on May 23 the details of a tap issue, either a new bond or a re-opening of an existing state loan, with first subscriptions on May 27.
